text.p: Leading stories in the Greek press:
TA NEA
--Prime Minister and PASOK leader Costas Simitis won
last Friday's televised debate with main challenger Miltiades
Evert, according to Metron Analysis opinion poll.
Best presence: Simitis 46.4 percent, Evert 33.7, neither 16.3
Best arguments: Simitis 40.4, Evert 34.1, neither 22.7
Best prime minister: Simitis 38.2, Evert 27.4, neither 31.8
--Evert's spasmodic moves: New Democracy leader
continually changing election tactics.
ETHNOS
--Building the welfare state: Simitis targets growth
and social solidarity. "We have built solid foundations and
are already building the welfare state," he says in exclusive
interview.
--Evert fears television 'interrogation', cancelling
last night's scheduled appearance. The ND leader's moves betray
panic and have caused concern at party headquarters.
--Political Spring leader Antonis Samaras: Yes, to
collaboration but under conditions, in event of no majority
government.
--Communist leader Aleka Papariga refuses the kiss of
life to bipartisan politics at her party's impressive rally in
central Athens last night.
ELEFTHEROTYPIA
--Evert prepares television coup: ND has Evert ready to
speak to four television channels on Friday night, following
PASOK's Athens rally.
--Voters rally round PASOK. Increasing attendance at
rallies and recent polls show that disaffected voters are
returning to the fold of an increasingly optimistic PASOK
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS
--The need to take painful economic measures behind the
decision to call early elections, according to confidential
economy ministry report. Simitis plans brutal austerity for
KATHIMERINI
--Ruling party PASOK and main rival New Democracy up the
ante as election day nears. Emphasis on the disadvantages of
either party rather than on issues.
--PASOK leader Costas Simitis pledges to support the
price of cotton in the budget, at party rally in Larissa.
--Slight pressure on drachma, due to pre-election
period. Bank of Greece unconcerned and says exchange policy will
be unchanged.
--New fuel and diesel prices expected to be announced
today by the Public Fuel Organisation (DEP).
--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou says
Parnitha casino will remain under the control of the state.
IMERISIA
--Parties enter the final stretch to election day. PASOK
optimistic that it has regrouped 73 percent of supporters from
last elections. New Democracy looks to have the last word with
leader Miltiades Evert's televised interview on Friday,
following Simitis's address at the main PASOK rally in Athens.
--Financing for Public Investment Programme for
first eight months of 1996 stands at 700 billion drachmas.
--Decline in state revenues for August. Rate of increase
of tax revenues at 11 percent, down from the revised forecast of
14.5 percent. January-August receipts increased 12.5 percent.
EXPRESS
--Parties agree increased growth the key to healthy
economy.
--Fall in state revenues and public spending concerns
finance ministry.
--Public Power Company (DEH) clinches 250 million dollar
syndicated loan.
--EU's Leader II programme to inject 81.7 billion
drachmas into rural Greece.
KERDOS
--New government faces intensifying efforts to increase
state revenues for the remaining quarter.
--Parnitha casino to be managed by private sector but
state will retain control, Development Minister Vasso Papandreou
says.
--National Mortgage Bank moves to sell off real estate
holdings.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Overspending and missing revenue targets threaten the
achievement of 1996 budget targets.
--All parties pledge to support small and medium-size
enterprises at last night's Biotechnical Chamber of Greece
event.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
